subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the design for an armored wheeled riot-control vehicle, roughly 5.6m long and 2.4m wide, deciding on wheel count and axle layout as a static model facing forward.

Since this is a static model without rigging, I'm planning to build it with unjointed parts attached at the root, using box and cylinder helpers to construct the chassis, body, and sloped hood. I'm also figuring out materials from the clockwork kit (panelled, metal, glow) and plotting out add-ons like the roof water cannon turret, neon light bars, corporate logo decals, plow bumper, slit windows, headlights, side skirts, ladder, shield plates, spotlights, and antenna, grounding wheel centers at y=0.55.

Switching from a frustum-based hood to an extruded cabin profile instead, defining a polygon outline in z-y coordinates to shape the sloped windshield, roof, and rear of the cab.

Working out the windshield tilt angle so the glass box aligns with the slope between those two points, then nudging it slightly outward along its normal for clearance.

Now I'm placing slit-style side windows along the vehicle's flanks, and thinking through how to orient decal planes on the doors so any logo text would face outward correctly from each side.

Adding the barrel and nozzle with a glowing cyan tip, then sizing a rear water tank cylinder and adjusting the cab length so the tank fits over the back deck without making the truck too tall.

Building the turret with a rotating base, boxy housing, a slightly elevated main cannon rod with a flared nozzle, and a glowing torus ring at the barrel tip...

Adding neon accent strips...

Now I'm placing the headlights with a cyan-white glow and magenta DRL strip, plus a dark grille with horizontal slats and a front bumper with hazard striping on a push-bar design. For the wheels, I'm working out six-wheel positioning along the tank body with axle placement at different z-depths and consistent radius and width.

Still positioning wheels and fenders...

I'm figuring out the chassis underbelly dimensions, then setting up a graphite/steel panelled paint scheme with rivets for the body armor, plus corporate branding -- an "ARMADYNE" shield emblem and "RIOT SUPPRESSION UNIT" door text.

I'm planning five decal textures: the door logo, a tank stencil reading "H₂O CONTROL," hazard stripes, a license plate, and a windshield HUD banner, then projecting them onto the body surfaces using positioned decal calls with direction and size parameters.

I'm reasoning through decal orientation on curved tank surfaces versus flat planes, deciding to just use plane geometry for the door emblems and simple decals for the tank sides without worrying about mirroring, then figuring out the x-coordinates where cab and body panels sit relative to center.

Now I'm placing the body logo plane near the door area and setting its viewBox dimensions. I'm also planning extra greebling details like roof antennas, camera domes, sirens, spotlight clusters, mirrors, door handles, a rear ladder, tow hooks, and exhaust stacks to add visual complexity to the truck model.

I want to add a windshield cage made of slanted rods for an armored look, plus a rear bumper, tail light strips, and possibly riot-shield plates along the tank sides with hazard decals -- while skipping extras like drones or hover-thrusters to keep the design grounded.

Adding box, cylinder, and glow helper functions, with mirrored neon strips in cyan and magenta along the skirts for underglow.

For the windshield HUD I'm designing a dark teal gradient screen with scanlines and glowing "SUSPECT: COMPLIANT?" text, dialing the glow down low. I'm also sketching a tank water-level display with a percentage bar, and planning the ARMADYNE logo as a magenta shield emblem with bold white lettering and a cyan subtitle, using dark outlines for legibility.

Now I'm fleshing out more SVG assets -- a hydro-pacifier tank label with a cyan fill bar and fine-print warning text, a yellow license plate reading "NC-7734", and yellow/black hazard stripe patterns built from rotated polygons. I decide to skip kanji-style signage since the characters won't render reliably, opting for plain ASCII instead, then move to writing the actual component code, keeping it around 350 lines and double-checking the extrude API calls for the cab geometry.

Working through the extrusion math, I confirm the axis orientation works out, and I note no smoothing is needed on the sharp corners. I place the grille and headlights on the front fascia, add a thin magenta glow strip along the hood's roofline, then work out how to orient the wheel torus and cylinder geometries so their rotation axes line up correctly, adding a glowing rim ring on the outer face.

Adding wheel hub details...

Working out the barrel's angled geometry and positioning the nozzle ring at its end point...

Now I'm positioning the tank body with banded tori along its length, then figuring out how to cap its end with a dome-shaped partial sphere oriented to face outward.

Adding tank decals on both sides, then moving to rear details: a red glowing tail strip and a rear ladder built from vertical rods.

I catch a geometry mistake — the dome cap at the tank's rear end would extend too far past the body if centered where I had it, so I shift the cylinder to end at -2.5 and squash the dome's scale on the z-axis to keep it flush with the body around -2.72. I drop the ladder idea in favor of a rear hatch instead.

Dropping the ladder entirely in favor of a simple rear step bumper, I now move to finalizing the paint scheme: graphite panels for the body, white countershaded panels for the cab, and a white tank with magenta accent bands for a two-tone look.
